clue.text: Good news about old boy that was poorly hidden

parts.note: OB is the usual abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil of a school
the good news about someone who was ill is that he's cured, so this phrase with 'that was poorly' supplies 'S CURED after the old boy

explanation.surface: A news bulletin about a former pupil's illness turns out to have been poorly concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Good news about old boy that was poorly' as the bulletin itself: OB'S CURED. The words 'that was poorly' explain why being cured is the news, and the apostrophe vanishes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscured is covered up or concealed from view, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Bank building nothing in English city on river

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it, so the river follows
the zero is placed in the middle of the city's name, splitting it after its first letter

parts.note: BATH is a spa city in Somerset, England
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing
the OUSE is the name of several English rivers, one flowing through York

explanation.surface: A building put up in an English city beside its river, with nothing inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is not a financial house here but a riverbank, which is where such a building stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A boathouse is a shed built on a riverbank for storing boats, so it is literally a building on the bank.

clue.text: Land in south-east Europe, having changed at Cairo

indicators.note: the letters of the two words that follow 'having' are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone arrives in a Balkan country after a change of planes at Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' sounds like changing flights at Cairo airport, but it tells you to rearrange AT CAIRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a Balkan country on the Adriatic, in the south-east of the continent.

clue.text: Divide by radius to get X or y, so to speak

definitions.text: X or y, so to speak

parts.note: to rive is an old word meaning to split or tear apart
R is the standard abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: A mathematics problem: divide by the radius to find the value of x or y.
explanation.walkthrough: X and Y spoken aloud are EXE and WYE, two British rivers (the Exe in Devon, the Wye on the Welsh border). 'by' simply sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exe and the Wye are both British watercourses, and the letters x and y sound like their names.

clue.text: Point I, in other case, must get over

definitions.meaning: a small round mark or spot, as in a decimal point

definitions.text: I, in other case, must get over
definitions.meaning: a capital letter I written in lower case needs a little mark placed above it

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on where the letter I must go when its case changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is not grammatical case (I becoming ME) but typographic case: lower-case i carries a mark over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a tiny point, and it is the mark that sits over a lower-case i.

clue.text: Every year, fast held in ecclesiastical office

indicators.note: the blog notes 'held' signals the two pieces are kept together side by side rather than one inside the other

parts.note: PA is short for per annum, Latin for each year
pacy means quick, having plenty of pace

explanation.surface: Every year a fast is observed by holders of a church office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as a religious fast, fitting the church setting, but it is the adjective meaning quick.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the office of Pope, the highest position in the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Standard drink maid assembled, one serving person at the bar

definitions.text: one serving person at the bar

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in 'up to par'
ale is beer, a common drink
a maid is a girl, informally a gal

explanation.surface: A barmaid puts together a standard drink for a customer at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a pub, with a maid serving at the bar; but 'the bar' is the legal profession, and 'assembled' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A paralegal is a trained assistant who supports lawyers, and barristers belong to the Bar.

clue.text: Possibly Pakistani joke to poke India on radio

parts.note: a pun is a joke playing on words
to jab is to poke sharply
India is the radio code word for the letter I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A Pakistani comedian makes a joke on the radio to needle India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on radio' looks like a sound signal, but it points to the radio alphabet, where India stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjabi describes a person from the Punjab, a region divided between Pakistan and India, so a Pakistani may be one.

clue.text: Rounding up leaders of criminals in raids, cops act roughly

indicators.note: gathering the leading letters of the next five words collects their initials in order

explanation.surface: In police raids, officers act rough when rounding up the gang's leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: The police story hides that you simply gather the first letters of 'criminals in raids, cops act'.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa, Latin for 'around', is used before a date or number to mean approximately.

clue.text: Ancient role, one in the past

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
ago means before now, in the past

explanation.surface: An actor recalls a classical part he once played long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' is not 'very old' but an old military rank (ensign): in Othello this villain is Othello's ancient.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Othello, the schemer holds the rank of ensign, called 'ancient', so the part is that of an ancient.

clue.text: Not the kind of surgeon you would want, confusing artery and vein

definitions.text: Not the kind of surgeon you would want

indicators.note: mixing up the two blood vessels' names jumbles their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A surgeon who confuses an artery with a vein is not one you would want operating on you.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is humorous: a vet is a fine surgeon for an animal, just not the one you would want for yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: A veterinary surgeon treats animals, so a human patient would not want one operating.

clue.text: A lot richer when corrupted, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: corrupting something distorts it, so the letters of the three words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Becoming much richer goes with being corrupted, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like the usual phrase meaning 'so to speak', but here it literally describes the art of persuasive speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetorical means relating to rhetoric, the art and style of public speaking and persuasion.

clue.text: Most important, as he is in Manchester, not rotherham or Sheffield

definitions.meaning: chief, principal, at the heart of things

definitions.text: as he is in Manchester, not rotherham or Sheffield
definitions.meaning: the letters H and E sit at the exact middle of the ten letters of Manchester, but off-centre in the other two towns

explanation.surface: A northerner claims he matters most in Manchester rather than in rival Yorkshire towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Count letters: in MANCHESTER, HE are the fifth and sixth of ten, the middle pair; in ROTHERHAM and SHEFFIELD they are off-centre. All three are cities in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something central is principal or key, and also sits in the middle position.

clue.text: Not to back Asian ruler could be a shock

indicators.note: to back here means to turn round, so the ruler's title is read from right to left

parts.note: a raja is an Indian prince or king

explanation.surface: Refusing to support an Asian ruler might come as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not to' means a door not shut, slightly open. 'could be a shock' gives a second wordplay: A + JAR (a jolt), so the answer is reached two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is not pushed to, i.e. not fully closed, is slightly open.

clue.text: Cut expected share for a period

indicators.note: cutting a word here docks its final letter

parts.note: due means expected, as in 'the train is due'
a ration is a fixed share or allowance

explanation.surface: Someone's expected share is cut for a period, like rationing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a reduction to someone's allowance, fitting 'share', but it only docks the final letter of the word for expected.
explanation.definitionFit: A duration is the length of time something lasts, a stretch or span.

clue.text: Put in new measures and vote in reforms

indicators.note: reforming something remakes it, so the letters of the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A government brings in new laws and votes in reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' looks like a noun in the political scene, but it is the verb telling you to rearrange AND VOTE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To innovate is to introduce new methods or ideas, putting fresh measures in place.

clue.text: Finish off good fruit, producing hiccup

indicators.note: finishing off the fruit here means taking away its final letter

parts.note: a litchi (or lychee) is a sweet Chinese fruit

explanation.surface: Polishing off some good fruit produces an attack of hiccups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' looks like eating it all up, but it means removing the last letter from LITCHI.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a minor setback or snag, which is what a hiccup means figuratively.

clue.text: Superficial damage when Tory leader replaces female in turmoil

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another within the word for turmoil

parts.note: confusion is a state of turmoil or disorder

indicators.note: a leader is the first in line, so only the opening letter of Tory is used

explanation.surface: A political row in which a Tory leader replaces a woman causes some bruising.
explanation.walkthrough: The political drama hides that T (the first letter of Tory) takes the place of F in CONFUSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A contusion is a bruise, an injury that harms the surface without breaking the skin.

clue.text: Perfect bliss European found in ashram

indicators.note: the single letter is discovered sitting inside the word for a retreat

parts.note: an ashram is a spiritual retreat, a haven or refuge

explanation.surface: A European finds perfect bliss in an Indian spiritual retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: An ashram is a Hindu religious retreat; here it stands for any place of refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven is used figuratively for a state of supreme happiness or delight.

clue.text: All the same, it's not kind

definitions.meaning: diversity is the opposite of everything being identical
a sort or type, as in a new strain of rose

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that, nevertheless, a remark wasn't very generous.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma tempts you to read 'All the same' as 'nevertheless' and 'kind' as 'generous'; in fact the first four words are one definition and 'kind' (a type) the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety means diversity, the absence of sameness, and also a type or sort.

clue.text: Material about part of Med

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
the Levant is the eastern Mediterranean coast and its lands

explanation.surface: A document about the eastern part of the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like a noun (cloth, matter) but is the adjective meaning pertinent, as in 'material evidence'.
explanation.definitionFit: Material, in the legal sense, means pertinent or significant to the matter at hand.

clue.text: Stove's lit after removing top for meat

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: a stove is an oven, and 's here stands for 'is'
a lit lamp or cooker is switched on

explanation.surface: Once the stove is lit, the cook takes the top off to cook meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Stove's lit' as OVEN IS ON; removing the top letter O leaves VEN IS ON. 'after' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is the flesh of deer eaten as food.

clue.text: Vessel held by crew erratically going either way

indicators.note: the run of letters can be read in either direction and still give the jug, so it works backwards as well as forwards
the answer is contained within the letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A ship's vessel is held by a crew who steer it erratically back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: cREW ERratically holds the four letters reading forwards from the E, and reading backwards from the second R; hence 'going either way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug or pitcher, a container for water.

clue.text: Expression of delight by learner, in turn

parts.note: whee is a cry of excitement or delight, as on a fairground ride
L, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner shouts with delight on taking their turn.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to swing round or pivot, as soldiers wheel on parade.

clue.text: Large — very light with nothing in

indicators.note: the zero is placed inside the combination of the other two pieces

parts.note: luminous means giving off light, bright
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Something large but very light, with nothing in it, like a balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like the opposite of large (weightless) but means shining.
explanation.definitionFit: Voluminous means occupying great space, ample or capacious.

clue.text: Article appearing under novelist's name is unexpected benefit

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece appearing under another is written after it

parts.note: Thomas Mann was a German novelist, author of The Magic Mountain
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article published under a novelist's name brings an unexpected windfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' sounds like a newspaper piece but is the grammatical article A, placed below MANN.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna, the food from heaven in Exodus, is used for any windfall or godsend.

clue.text: A president oddly lacking inspiration

indicators.note: behaving oddly, the letters of the two words take on a strange new arrangement

explanation.surface: A president is criticised for being oddly lacking in inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' reads as an adverb on the president's dullness, but it tells you to rearrange A PRESIDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian, used figuratively, means dull, commonplace and uninspired.

clue.text: Hostile? The reason's clear to me, you might say

indicators.note: spoken out loud the words sound like the answer's letters

parts.note: 'I see' is what you say when something's reason becomes clear

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a reaction was hostile, and says the reason is now plain.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying 'I see' gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy manner is cold and unfriendly, as in an icy stare.

clue.text: Swindle family, son first

indicators.note: placing the son first puts his letter at the front, before family

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
kin means one's family or relations

explanation.surface: Someone swindles their own family, putting their son first.
explanation.walkthrough: To skin someone is slang for fleecing or cheating them.
explanation.definitionFit: To skin someone, informally, is to cheat them out of money, to fleece them.

clue.text: Put on pitch, outside left took part in game

indicators.note: the word for tarring sits outside the abbreviation for left, enclosing it

parts.note: to pay, in old nautical usage, is to coat a ship's seams with pitch or tar

explanation.surface: A player is put on the pitch at outside left and takes part in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' is not a sports field but tar, and 'outside left' is not a football position but an instruction to put the word for tar around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To have played is to have participated in a match or sport.

clue.text: Telling tales about eastern desire

indicators.note: the word for storytelling goes round the letter for eastern, enclosing it

parts.note: yarning means spinning yarns, telling stories

explanation.surface: Telling tales about the East reveals a longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling tales' suggests snitching, but here it is telling yarns, stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearning is a deep longing or wish for something.
